defs_parts: Seven labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Video only: the term comes from a video lecture, and is not in the course text or on the term list.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A material is values per pixel, and lighting turns them into colour.
Roughness runs from mirror to dull, and smoothness runs the other way.
Only the base colour is decoded from sRGB, the other maps are data.
A normal map fakes bumps, and Godot expects green pointing up.
An ORM map packs occlusion, roughness and metallic into red, green and blue.
Texel density, not resolution, decides how sharp a texture looks on a surface.
bookends.command: Quiz me on material and texture terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use albedo, roughness, smoothness, colour texture, data texture, normal map, ORM, SSAO, texel density and mipmap. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
